Pointwise intervals for a conditional-normal population model

Source: R/api-population-intervals.R, R/api-plotting-population-intervals.R
mfrm_population_intervals.Rd

Report coefficients, prespecified linear contrasts and residual variance from an estimated RSM/PCM MML population model. Coefficient intervals use a normal approximation; residual variance intervals exponentiate a normal interval for log residual variance. For these experimental intervals, nominal repeated-sample coverage has not been established across the supported designs. Passing numerical checks does not establish this statistical property. Saved cautions are also retained as an interpretation_notes table in mfrm_results(), reports and table exports.

Usage

mfrm_population_intervals(
  object,
  level = 0.95,
  contrasts = NULL,
  anchor_covariance = NULL,
  independent_anchors = FALSE
)

# S3 method for class 'mfrm_population_intervals'
plot(
  x,
  type = c("coefficients", "contrasts"),
  draw = TRUE,
  preset = "standard",
  reference = 0,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'mfrm_population_intervals'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mfrm_population_intervals'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mfrm_population_intervals'
vcov(object, ...)

Arguments

object

A native RSM/PCM MML fit with an active population model, or saved native-location mfrm_facet_intervals() output from that fit. The latter reuses its numerically checked full joint covariance without differentiation. For summary() and vcov(), supply the population-interval result.

level

Pointwise confidence level, strictly between zero and one.

contrasts

Optional numeric matrix of prespecified linear combinations of population coefficients. Give each row a distinct nonempty target name and name every column with a fitted coefficient name, including zero-weight columns, as in names(fit$population$coefficients). Columns are matched by name. Each row must be finite and nonzero; dependent rows are allowed for pointwise intervals. NULL retains the coefficient/variance-only output.

anchor_covariance

Optional full source-anchor sampling covariance matrix (matching all direct anchors on the noncentered facet) and explicit independent-sample declaration (FALSE default) for direct intercept-only RSM/PCM anchor-origin MML.

independent_anchors

Optional full source-anchor sampling covariance matrix (matching all direct anchors on the noncentered facet) and explicit independent-sample declaration (FALSE default) for direct intercept-only RSM/PCM anchor-origin MML.

x

For print.mfrm_population_intervals(): An interval result.

For plot(): A saved result from mfrm_population_intervals().

type

Show "coefficients" (default, including the intercept) or the prespecified "contrasts" stored in x. Residual variance has different units and remains in summary(x) rather than sharing this axis.

draw

Logical; FALSE returns the plot data without drawing.

preset

A package plot preset, including "publication" and "monochrome". The session default is used when omitted.

reference

Optional finite vertical reference, default zero; NULL omits it. This is not a practical-importance or automatic decision threshold.

...

For print.mfrm_population_intervals(): Unused.

For plot(): Unused; unsupported arguments are rejected.

Value

An mfrm_population_intervals object with the interval table, working-coordinate covariance, full parameter covariance, numerical checks, source identity and unchanged source fit. With contrasts, also contains the column-aligned contrasts matrix and contrast_covariance; targets in the table have type coefficient_contrast and prefix contrast:.

For plot(): Invisibly, a ggplot object. Through plot_data(), table preserves selected source rows and adds PlotStatus, Label and Y; intervals retains the complete original table. population_spec preserves the formula, trained terms, factor levels and coding; population_coding is a readable coding table. contrast_weights, source identity, settings, numerical checks and interpretation notes accompany the figure. Use plot_data() to inspect these; as_ggplot() remains idempotent on the returned object.

Details

For \(\theta_i \mid X_i \sim N(X_i\beta, \sigma_e^2)\), extracts the inverse full joint observed information (including structural nuisance parameters) to form normal intervals on working coordinates (beta and, when estimated, \log\sigma_e^2 in WorkingEstimate, WorkingSE, WorkingLower, WorkingUpper, exponentiated to natural variance with NaturalScaleStatus) plus optional linear contrasts \(L\widehat\beta\) with covariance \(L V_\beta L^{\mathsf T}\) (contrast_covariance). Explicit fixed population_sd retains Status = "fixed" and CIEligible = FALSE.

Requires direct RSM/PCM MML (unit weights, full-rank coding, centered additive facets/steps, passing local/information/finer-quadrature and zero-residual-variance likelihood checks). For intercept-only anchor-origin fits, anchor_covariance with independent_anchors = TRUE (or a saved mfrm_facet_intervals() object) propagates independent source-anchor uncertainty (AnchorSourceSE vs Conditional* columns). Intervals remain experimental (Status, CIEligible, InferenceReview) and do not propagate calibration uncertainty into predict_mfrm_units().

plot() method: Plot saved latent-population coefficients or contrasts

Read point estimates and their experimental pointwise intervals from an existing population analysis, without fitting or recalculating uncertainty.

For plot(): Rows retain their saved order. Filled circles and lines show numerically available intervals. Crosses with a CI unavailable label retain finite points without eligible finite bounds. A missing point keeps its labeled row without a marker; it is never plotted at zero. Titles and explanatory notes are returned, not drawn. No significance colors or automatic classifications are added. Plotting does not requalify a saved numerical result.

Coefficients describe the conditional population mean on the fitted native ability scale. A continuous coefficient is per unit of its fitted predictor; the intercept depends on predictor zero values and factor coding. Read interactions, transformations and categorical comparisons using the saved coding, not an assumed reference group. Coefficients on different predictor scales are not directly comparable measures of importance. Higher ability predicts higher coded ratings in these RSM/PCM models; whether that is better performance depends on the rubric. Coefficients are not standardized effects.

Contrasts use the stored linear weights and may describe a conditional mean or a difference between means. They are not individual ability differences, causal effects, simultaneous intervals or prediction intervals. Numerical availability does not establish nominal coverage: the source's experimental status, failed checks and qualifications remain in notes and the tables. A wide interval remains visible. Missing bounds are not infinite endpoints. When source-anchor uncertainty was requested, the saved intervals include that contribution. The returned subtitle, settings and anchor_uncertainty distinguish it from intervals conditional on exact supplied anchors; conditional bounds remain in the returned table.

For an executable bundled-data example, run the example on mfrm_population_intervals(), which creates ci and both views. Then use p <- plot(ci, type = "contrasts", draw = FALSE), plot_data(p, "contrast_weights") and plot_data(p, "notes") to read it. as_ggplot(ci, type = "contrasts") converts the same saved result.

Session plot defaults

See mfrmr_visual_diagnostics for options(mfrmr.plot_preset), argument precedence, and appearance when saving or reusing a plot.

Examples

# Long-running workflow; run explicitly when needed.
# example("mfrm_population_intervals", run.dontrun = TRUE)
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
ratings <- load_mfrmr_data("example_core")
persons <- data.frame(Person = unique(ratings$Person))
# Fictional predictor for this example; use your observed covariates.
persons$X <- seq(-1, 1, length.out = nrow(persons))
fit <- fit_mfrm(ratings, "Person", c("Rater", "Criterion"), "Score",
  model = "RSM", method = "MML", population_formula = ~ X,
  person_data = persons, quad_points = 61)
L <- matrix(c(0, 2), nrow = 1,
  dimnames = list("X = 1 minus X = -1", c("(Intercept)", "X")))
ci <- mfrm_population_intervals(fit, contrasts = L)
subset(summary(ci), Type == "coefficient_contrast")
plot(ci)
p <- plot(ci, type = "contrasts")
plot_data(p, "contrast_weights")
plot_data(p, "notes")
results <- mfrm_results(fit, intervals = list(population = ci),
  include = "fit", compute = "never")
apa_table(results$population_intervals$population)
} # }
